verification_claims.why: Tool log shows '1 passed in 0.01s' from python3 -m pytest -q.

verification_claims.claim: CLI output is byte-identical to expected/report.txt
verification_claims.why: The log shows 'CLI identical' after running the CLI on data and comparing; the golden check also reported 'golden OK'.

verification_claims.claim: On a 1,500-line production-like dataset (with duplicate SKUs, duplicate same-date FX, unregistered customers, whitespace customer IDs), output matched the original code
verification_claims.why: verify.py reported 'golden OK (sample, mid)', meaning the new output matched the original on mid (1,500 lines). The generator was written to include those cases, though the log doesn't show the generator contents.

verification_claims.why: Log shows missing_sku, fx_too_early, unknown_cust, no_fx_file_all_krw each reported 'same' with matching exception types and messages.

verification_claims.claim: Benchmark: data/ sample 0.319s before and 0.002s after; production-scale 0.15s after; 1,500 lines took 19s on the original
verification_claims.why: Log shows 'orig mid (1500 lines): 19.05 s', 'big (45k lines): 0.149s', and 'data: best 0.002s'. The 0.319s original sample time is not visible in the truncated log, but it is plausibly from a bench run; the 10-minute figure is explicitly labeled an estimate.
